title: haldia petrochemicals aims use more lpg iran war threatens feedstock supplies 2026 09 09
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 9 (Reuters) - India's Haldia Petrochemicals is looking to increase liquefied petroleum gas substitution at its naphtha-fed cracker to as much ​as 30% to hedge against supply risks from the Middle ‌East due to the U.S.-Iran war, its chief executive said on Wednesday.
"We are working with Lummus to retrofit our cracker with LPG flexibility of up to ​30%," Navanit Narayan told Reuters on the sidelines of the ​APPEC industry conference.
Naphtha and LPG are key petrochemicals feedstocks used ⁠to make plastics and automotive parts.
"The (naphtha) supply shock from Gulf war ​was a wake up call for us, we will have a ​plan ready by the end of the year," Narayan said.
Haldia has term contracts with QatarEnergy, Kuwait Petroleum Corp and ADNOC Global Trading for naphtha supplies, but had ​to turn to the spot market after shipments through the Strait ​of Hormuz came to a near standstill.
"We have been able to land some medium-range ‌cargoes ⁠at Vizag from United Arab Emirates, still trying to get Qatari volumes out," Narayan said. A medium-range tanker can carry up to 35,000 metric tons of oil products.
Narayan said the company would source LPG domestically ​from Indian Oil ​Petronas Limited (IPPL), ⁠which operates a plant next to HPL at the same site.
"We are also looking to import LPG from ​every available source," he added.
Haldia operates a 700,000 ​ton-per-year ethylene ⁠plant, with annual chemical processing capacity of 491,000 tons and polymer processing capacity of about 1 million tons at its manufacturing facility in the ⁠eastern ​state of West Bengal. It plans to ​inaugurate an acetone and phenol plant in October.
The company is majority owned by U.S.-based private ​equity firm The Chatterjee Group.
